correctness.rationale: The Reid--Roberts--Vitulli theorem reduces three-variable monomial normality to integral closedness through the second power. Every possible second-power hole reduces to an x-exponent-one factorization, equivalent to whether the two-generator numerical semigroup meets one explicit interval. Even product bc is immediately normal. For odd noncoprime b,c, a Frobenius-bound semigroup point lies in every interval. For odd coprime b,c, exactly one of the adjacent midpoint integers lies in the semigroup, giving the iff classification and explicit hole. An independent finite replay of the exact interval criterion over thousands of pairs found no mismatch.

originality.rationale: Reid--Roberts--Vitulli provide the general second-power criterion, a necessary semigroup condition in the pairwise-coprime corner setting, and the example with exponents 2, 3, and 7, but not the complete exponent-two iff classification. Later accessible work gives broader criteria or sufficient conditions rather than this all-pairs arithmetic theorem.

value.rationale: This completely classifies a natural infinite two-parameter slice of a published three-variable normality problem, explains a classical counterexample by a general arithmetic mechanism, and gives explicit witnesses for every failure.
